 Harrisburg, Pa. — The Mansfield campus of Commonwealth University, formerly known as Mansfield University, is set to close in 2028, officials announced.
 Following a comprehensive analysis identifying significant enrollment and financial challenges at the Mansfield campus of Commonwealth University, Pennsylvania's State System of Higher Education (PASSHE) Chancellor Christopher Fiorentino directed the university to develop a framework for the orderly wind-down of campus operations by June 30, 2028.
 “Planning now for an orderly wind-down of operations at the Mansfield campus will put Commonwealth University on a stronger path to long-term success and better position it to continue providing a relevant, rigorous and affordable education to students," said Chancellor Fiorentino. “Our top priority through this process is that students at the Mansfield campus have a path to finish their degree at Commonwealth University.”
 In July, Chancellor Fiorentino requested that Commonwealth University conduct a comprehensive analysis of enrollment, finances, regional demographics and infrastructure needs at its three campuses — CU-Bloomsburg, CU-Lock Haven and CU-Mansfield. That analysis was shared with the chancellor, statewide unions and the Commonwealth University community in October.
 The Mansfield campus enrolled 1,013 students in fall 2026, a 71.6% decline since 2009. Enrollment is projected to decline by another 20% by 2028 as the pool of prospective students in the region shrinks. The campus lost $7,825 per full-time-equivalent student in 2025-26, part of a $7.72 million deficit, creating mounting financial challenges that are straining Commonwealth University's finances.
 Based on the analysis and in consultation with Board of Governors leadership, Chancellor Fiorentino directed Commonwealth University President Jeffery Osgood to develop a framework for the orderly wind-down of operations at the Mansfield campus by June 30, 2028. The framework must be submitted to the chancellor by Dec. 8, 2026.
 “I understand how deeply people care about Mansfield and how difficult this will be for those who have dedicated years of their lives to the campus,” said Chancellor Fiorentino. “That history and the people connected to it, including today’s students, will be respected.
 “I also want to recognize the hard work that students, faculty and staff across Commonwealth University have done and continue to do to build the university’s future. A wind-down at Mansfield will not be easy, but taking this action amid changes across higher education is necessary to best serve students."
 The framework will address how the university will enable students at the Mansfield campus to graduate from Commonwealth University, minimize employee losses to the greatest extent possible and address the economic impact on the community.
 “PASSHE has a responsibility to safeguard the sustainability of the entire State System so our universities can continue providing a high-quality, affordable education to students across Pennsylvania for years to come,” said Cynthia Shapira, chair of the Board of Governors. “That requires confronting difficult challenges while recognizing and mitigating, to the extent possible, the impact these decisions have on people. I know that the university will prioritize students’ ability to complete their degrees at Commonwealth University and work to help employees during this transition.”
 Closure of the Mansfield campus requires authorization by the Board of Governors due to the nature of its integration action in 2021. An authorization vote would occur at a future public meeting. After that, appropriate documentation would be provided to the Pennsylvania Department of Education per state regulations to initiate the formal closure of the campus.
 Commonwealth University is communicating directly with students and employees.
